name: sam_baselines
registered: 2026-11-11, before any run of these rows on a real scene (only one-frame smoke tests of the code had run)
asked_by: user, 2026-11-11: re-implement LangSplat and OpenGaussian 'in our protocol' as extra rows next to the re-implemented Feature 3DGS and LEGaussians
question: How do two SAM-mask feature-lifting methods, LangSplat and OpenGaussian, compare with the other rows of Tables I, II, III, IV and the error-split table when they lift the same 2D features on the same map?
shared_protocol: As every row of papers/main.tex 'Maps and baselines': the scene's fixed 3D-GS map (geometry frozen), the main field's mapping frames (scripts/distill_features.py select_frames), the LSeg features compressed by the field's own PCA to d = 64 (unit vectors), the splat-weight renderer, the coverage floor tau_cov = 0.5 and scripts/eval_seg.py's evaluation (text cosine -> softmax over the scene's classes, one temperature per row fitted on validation). The methods' own ingredient is SAM: their CLIP feature per mask is replaced by the unit mean of the LSeg PCA-64 features inside the mask, so every row sees the same 2D features.

langsplat.paper: Qin et al., LangSplat, CVPR 2024, arXiv 2312.16084
langsplat.definition: usplat/sam_lift.py (h): a scene autoencoder 64 -> 3 (its autoencoder/model.py scaled to 64-d: encoder 64-32-16-8-3 with BatchNorm + ReLU, decoder 3-8-16-32-64 with ReLU, unit outputs), trained on the mask features of all four SAM levels of the scene (its _f.npy holds default, s, m, l) with its loss l2_loss + 0.001 cos_loss (the cosine over the batch dimension, dim 0, as its code); Adam 1e-4, 100 epochs, batch 64, the lowest-loss epoch of the last 5. One model per level s, p, w: a per-Gaussian 3-d latent (zero init) trained with its l1_loss on the masked maps (|F - E(zbar)| summed over the covered pixels inside a mask, divided by all pixels x 3 channels); Adam lr 0.0025. Query: rendered latent -> decoder -> 64-d -> as every feature row. No uncertainty of its own (the evaluator's 1 - max p).

opengs.paper: Wu et al., OpenGaussian, NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2406.02058
opengs.definition: usplat/sam_lift.py (i), on the default-level masks (its ScanNet script: --sam_level 0): (a) per-Gaussian 6-d instance feature (unit, U[0,1) init) trained with L_c + 0.1 L_s (its cohesion_loss and separation_loss: 1 / (|m_i - m_j|^2 + 1) with its rank weights 0.1 + 0.9 rank / (m - 1), set to 0.1 below 0.9 after 5000 stage-1 iterations, its iteration 35k with stage 1 from 30k); every mask of the view with a covered pixel (its 50-px filter is commented out); Adam lr 0.001; (b) two-level codebook by k-means (10 rounds): k1 = 64 coarse clusters on [feature, 1.0 xyz], k2 = 5 fine clusters per coarse one on the feature (its ScanNet setting), 320 instances; (c) 2D-3D association per mapping view: instance mask = covered pixels where the instance's rendered share is >= 1/2 of alpha; best default-level SAM mask by S = IoU (1 - sum_k |c_ik - p_jk|) (its Eq. 5, calculate_pairwise_distances l1), a match needs S > 0.2; instance feature = the plain mean of the matched masks' pooled LSeg features over the views (its per_leaf_feat), unit at query (its F.normalize), zero when matched in fewer than 2 views (its eval_scannet.py occu_count < 2): uniform predictive. Query: per-Gaussian feature = its instance's feature, rendered, as every feature row. No uncertainty of its own.
opengs.settings_note: stage 1 capped at 30k with the stopping rule, the budget of every trained row; its ScanNet stage 1 is 20k (30k-50k)

methods.deviations: Listed in the usplat/sam_lift.py docstring ('Deviations from the papers and their code'), fixed with this registration. Shared protocol: LSeg PCA-64 mask means instead of CLIP per mask, SAM on the full frame with masks downscaled to the field's grid, losses on covered pixels only, views drawn with replacement, eval_seg's queries. LangSplat: widths scaled to 64-d, one level per row chosen on validation (it picks a level per query). OpenGaussian: plain k-means codebook without its stage-2 training, instance masks from the full map's splat weights, stage 1 capped at 30k (its ScanNet: 20k). SAM: an empty mask is dropped (a guard), mask_nms keeps the top 3 when no score passes (its code would raise there).

masks.levels: d (the fork's default stream: all three multimask outputs), s, p, w (its s, m, l: outputs 0, 1, 2), each through the same filters (predicted IoU > 0.7, stability >= 0.85, crop-edge boxes dropped, box NMS 0.7 per crop, cross-crop NMS 0.7 preferring smaller crops, SAM's clean-up of regions and holes < 100 px), then its masks_update (mask_nms on IoU_pred x stability: IoU 0.8, score 0.7, inner 0.5); painted in list order (a later mask overwrites an earlier one) at the field's grid (downscale 2: area average >= 1/2), int16, -1 = no mask
masks.frames: the main field's mapping frames; for Table IV also the update keyframes of the scene's Table III record (--table)
masks.outputs: results/sam_masks/<field stem>_sam.npz (mapping), results/sam_masks/<field stem>_sam_upd.npz (NOR update keyframes); labels (frames, 4, h, w)
masks.code_matched: segment-anything-langsplat segment_anything/automatic_mask_generator.py: generate, generate_curr_anns, _generate_masks, _generate_masks_data, _process_crop, _process_crop_data, _process_batch, _process_batch_data (usplat.sam_lift.LevelStreams on segment_anything 1.0); LangSplat preprocess.py: the SamAutomaticMaskGenerator arguments, sam_encoder, masks_update, mask_nms, filter, mask2segmap (usplat.sam_lift.make_generator, generate_levels, masks_update, mask_nms, paint_labels)
masks.identity: meta['identity'] = sha256 of the settings above, the model, the checkpoint sha256 and the mask code (LevelStreams, make_generator, mask_nms, masks_update, generate_levels, paint_labels, ...)

training.script: scripts/train_sam_baselines.py (imports scripts/distill_features.py and usplat/distill.py, never edits them)

main_fields.replica: the fields of configs/replica_val.json and configs/replica_test.json (results/fields/<scene>_lseg.pt)
main_fields.scannet: the fields of configs/scannet_val.json and configs/scannet_test.json (results/fields/scannet/<scene>_lseg.pt)

training.gpu: scripts/gpu_gate.sh 5000 (the extractor runs on the GPU as in distill_features.py)
training.identity: every file records sha256 identity of (code, the masks' settings identity, its config); eval_seg folds it into the scene identity (validation and test must match)

selection.langsplat_level: Per dataset (Replica, ScanNet): the level whose row (langsplat_s, langsplat_p, langsplat_w) has the highest mean mIoU ('all' pixels) over the validation scenes in the validation record eval_val.json below; ties -> the earlier level in (s, p, w) (scripts/sam_baselines_check.py select). The tables show that level's row; the other two are reported in the text or the report, never dropped silently.
selection.nor_level: Tables III and IV use the level chosen on Replica (no NOR-specific selection); only that level is trained on the NOR scenes.
selection.rule: Selection reads validation records only. Nothing is chosen on a test scene.

I (tab:replica).how: scripts/eval_seg.py with --row-factory usplat.baselines:row_factory,usplat.distill:row_factory,usplat.sam_lift:row_factory and Table I's arguments (Replica: --vocab configs/vocab_replica.json --extractor lseg --dataset replica_semnerf --stride 10 --downscale 2 --tau-cov 0.5 --text-cache <copy of results/fields/text_cache_lseg.pt>; ScanNet: --vocab configs/vocab_scannet.json --dataset scannet --stride 20, results/fields/scannet/text_cache_lseg.pt). Validation: --val-scenes = --scenes = the val config (fits the temperatures); test: --betas <that eval_val.json> --scenes <test config>.
I (tab:replica).rows: langsplat_s, langsplat_p, langsplat_w, opengs, and the controls ours_P0, ours_P2, normlift, f3dgs, legs_l4 (Replica) / legs_l1 (ScanNet), selected with --rows
I (tab:replica).cells: the chosen LangSplat level and OpenGaussian as two new rows (mIoU, accuracy, ECE, NLL, Brier, AURC; AUSE_u '--': no uncertainty of their own), marked re-implemented; bold / underline recomputed over all ranked rows; the CSS reference row stays unranked

tables.II (tab:perclass): Per-class IoU of the same two rows from the test records above (scripts/make_tables.py perclasspair, the same class columns); bold / underline recomputed.
tables.error split (tab:views): Only the full-map columns (Replica M = 180, ScanNet full): AUSE of 1 - max p relative to random, as the Feature 3DGS row, from the test records above (papers/table_tools/views_table.py's rule for trained rows); the M < 180 columns are '--' (no field from M frames).

III (tab:change).how: scripts/sam_change_nor.py change (scripts/eval_change_nor_distilled.py, imported unchanged) on each NOR scene with the scene's Table III record options (--align, --update-stride, --tau-cov from results/nor/tab2_relmax/<split>/<scene>.json, as scripts/nor_distilled.sh), --distilled <field>_langsplat_<Replica level>.pt,<field>_opengs.pt, --reference <the record>
III (tab:change).rows: langsplat_<level>_feat, opengs_feat: the feature residual (1 - cos of rendered and observed features) on their mapping-only features, frozen during the update, as the Feature 3DGS / LEGaussians rows of configs/nor_distilled_prereg.json

IV (tab:stale).how: train on the mapping AND update keyframes (train_sam_baselines.py --table, as configs/stale_baselines_prereg.json's f3dgs_upd / legs_l1_upd), then scripts/sam_change_nor.py stale (scripts/stale_baselines_nor.py, imported unchanged) --table <record> --dump results/qual/nor/<scene> --vocab configs/vocab_replica.json --text-cache results/stale_baselines/text_cache_lseg_nor.pt --distilled <field>_langsplat_<level>_upd.pt,<field>_opengs_upd.pt --stage <val|test> --no-2d
IV (tab:stale).rows: langsplat_<level>_upd, opengs_upd: the stale-answer rate (lower is better); the frozen mapping-only files may be added as reference rows (report only)
IV (tab:stale).validation: pipeline check only, as configs/stale_baselines_prereg.json: the trained pass on validation scene 002

controls.eval_seg: Every validation and test run recomputes the control rows (ours_P0, ours_P2, normlift, f3dgs, legs_l4 on Replica / legs_l1 on ScanNet). Every stored per-scene metric of the control rows must be within 0.005 absolute of the Table I record (results/tab1/eval_val.json, eval_test.json; results/scannet_tab1/eval_val.json, eval_test.json; rates as fractions, NLL in nats), and every fitted temperature within 1% relative; the run reports the max differences (scripts/sam_baselines_check.py control -> results/sam_baselines/<dataset>/control_<stage>.json). A failed check stops the driver before the next stage and is reported.
controls.change: The feat_control row of each Table III run is compared with the scene's Table III record (eval_change_nor_distilled.py --reference); max |diff| <= 1e-6, else stop.
controls.stale: The 'before' row must reproduce the scene's dump (stale_baselines_nor.py's stop rule: rate within 0.5 points, pixel count within 0.5%, else exit 2).
controls.code: tests/test_sam_lift.py: an OpenGaussian file with one instance per Gaussian holding the field's mu* gives the 'feat' row and the 'before' counts exactly (toy scene).
controls.eval_seg_note: Set before any run. The Replica Table I record was made on 2026-09-30 on the earlier machine and differs from a recompute on this machine by up to 3.0e-4 (ours rows 1.3e-5); ScanNet matches to 0. The measurement is in configs/perclass_ause_prereg.json control_amended (commit 9f0afbf).

test_policy: After the selection, each test scene runs once per table; a finished test record is never overwritten. Every row is reported, including scenes and metrics where a baseline beats ours. Nothing changes after the test run.
order: train (Replica + ScanNet val and test: three LangSplat levels, OpenGaussian)

budget.masks: about 4,800 frames: Replica 8 scenes x ~179 mapping frames (~1,430), ScanNet 10 scenes (2,110 mapping frames, distill logs), NOR 14 scenes (638 mapping + 637 update keyframes, configs/nor_val.json and nor_test.json counts). GPU time per frame: measured by the driver's time step before the full run (not measured yet; the crop layer makes SAM run on 5 crops per frame).
budget.trainings: 72 on Replica + ScanNet (18 scenes x 3 LangSplat levels + OpenGaussian) and 50 on NOR (14 mapping-only x 2, 11 mapping + update x 2); reference: Feature 3DGS took 28 ms/iter on Replica office_0 and 37-89 ms/iter on ScanNet (65 rendered channels), LangSplat renders 4 and OpenGaussian 7
budget.evaluations: eval_seg 4 runs (val, test x Replica, ScanNet), Table III 14 scene runs, Table IV 11 scene runs

code.unchanged: usplat/distill.py, usplat/rows.py, usplat/seg_eval.py, scripts/eval_seg.py, scripts/eval_change_nor_distilled.py, scripts/stale_baselines_nor.py and every file they import

revisions.before: any run of these rows (only one-frame smoke tests of the code had run)
revisions.change: Main-session decisions: follow each method's released code where it differs from its paper, unless that changes the shared protocol. SAM: LangSplat's real preprocessing (its fork's four-stream generator with one crop layer, its masks_update, list-order painting; levels d, s, p, w). OpenGaussian: the default level (its ScanNet --sam_level 0), the plain mean of the matched masks' features, its eval's >= 2 matched views, its L1-sum distance, its rank-weighted separation loss and no mask-size filter (its code). LangSplat: its autoencoder data (all four levels), its dim-0 cosine and its l1_loss normalization. eval_seg control tolerance set to 0.005 absolute / 1% relative (1e-6 cannot hold on Replica). Driver scripts/sam_baselines.sh with a SAM timing step.

driver.rules: Through scripts/gpu_gate.sh with UAGS_GPU_HEADROOM_MIB from the environment (default 1024); needs: masks 6000, training 5000, eval_seg 7000, Tables III/IV 6000 (need + headroom <= 8900, else refused). Resumable: finished outputs are skipped, a record with another status than ok is moved to the logs and rerun. Test steps refuse uncommitted changes in scripts/ usplat/ configs/; a finished test record is never overwritten. Logs: results/sam_baselines/logs/.
driver.time_step: SAM with the settings above on 2 frames of Replica office_0 on the GPU (gate 6000) -> results/sam_baselines/time/sam_time.json (s/frame of the second frame, the estimate for all frames); run before the masks step so the masks budget is measured.
